source.title: Open problems and conjectures: On the recursive sequence

trace.notes: Input normalized as a zbMATH resolver URL with identifier 1660668. A local index entry linked the record to DOI 10.1080/10236190108808283. Crossref and OpenAlex metadata confirmed the same exact work as a 2001 Journal of Difference Equations and Applications article, volume 7, issue 3, pages 477-482, with title "Open problems and conjectures" and subtitle "On the recursive sequence".

The supplied zbMATH page could not be used as a technical source: shell fetch returned a Cloudflare 403 challenge. The DOI resolved to the Taylor & Francis article page, but the abstract, PDF, and ePDF endpoints also returned Cloudflare 403 challenge pages. OpenAlex reported open_access.is_oa=false, best_oa_location=null, and no repository full text. Failure modes established: blocked_or_challenged for zbMATH and Taylor & Francis; paywalled_or_restricted and metadata_only for resolver records.

Bounded exact-work recovery attempted searches for the exact DOI, exact title plus PDF, exact title plus authors and pages, and the recursively defined sequence plus authors. Inspected candidates were rejected because they were the blocked publisher landing page, citation-only references in later papers, different papers that cite or discuss related difference equations, an open book preview bibliography, or search snippets without the article's problem statements. No readable exact-work PDF or full HTML source containing the problem statements was recovered.

No candidate questions were extracted because the workflow did not recover a readable primary technical source. Metadata, abstracts, citation references, and search snippets were not used as evidence for open-problem extraction.
Saved exact JSON to outputs/parse-paper/1660668.json and outputs/latest.json.
